structure: repos/trade-imports-reference-data is a small Java / Spring Boot service (about 1,650 lines of main code in scope, about 2,100 lines of unit and integration tests, about 1,000 lines of MDM JSON fixtures). It fronts MDM (the Defra master data service) and serves reference lists to the frontends through three REST endpoints: GET /countries (CountriesController, with an optional blocks filter and subdivisions), GET /ports-of-entry (PortsOfEntryController, with port types and list order), and GET /commodities plus POST /commodities/species-check (CommoditiesController, CommoditySearchService, SpeciesCheckService). Everything comes from MDM through MdmClient (Feign: /mdm/geo/countries, /mdm/trade/bcp/poes, /mdm/trade/product/search, /mdm/trade/product/commodities, /mdm/trade/product/commodities/{code}/species) and MdmService, with countries and ports cached (CacheConfig) and MDM failures mapped to HTTP errors by GlobalExceptionHandler and MdmErrorDecoder. Its rulings are the ADRs under doc/adr/ (0002: reference-data serves several domains until they get too large); there is no decisions ledger. Of the scope's seven lists, countries, ports, and commodities with species and commodity identifiers (commodity codes) are served today; transporters, document types and certification purposes have no endpoint, model or MDM call anywhere in the repo, so they are gaps. Left out as outside scope: metrics, observability, logging, tracing, TLS trust store, proxy, Mongo, AWS and auth-token plumbing (src/main/java/.../metrics, logging, filter, interceptor, configuration/tls and the non-MDM configuration classes) and CI workflows, except where they change what a caller receives. Cut into 3 parts by reference list: countries and ports; commodities and species; the service's shared contract (docs, ADRs, error handling, MDM configuration) together with the scope's missing lists.

parts.title: Countries and ports of entry
parts.scope: The GET /countries and GET /ports-of-entry endpoints: what each list returns, its fields, filters, order, subdivisions, port types and caching, and the MDM calls behind them. Stops at the commodity endpoints (part 2) and at the shared error handling (part 3). MdmService and MdmClient are shared: read in full, claim only their countries and ports methods.
covers: GET /countries: its route, every query parameter (the blocks filter and any other), every field of Country and SubDivision in the response, how MDM countries and blocks are mapped and filtered, the order the list comes back in, and what happens when MDM returns nothing
GET /ports-of-entry: its route, every query parameter, every field of PortOfEntry, every PortType value and how it is derived, the order PortListOrder gives, and how MDM ports are mapped and filtered
The countries and ports caches: their names, expiry, and the rule that empty results are not cached (MdmService getCountries and getPortsOfEntry, CacheConfig)
The MdmClient calls /mdm/geo/countries and /mdm/trade/bcp/poes with their parameters
Every test in the 9 test files listed that proves countries or ports behaviour (the MdmServiceTest countries and ports tests only), each as a claim of what is proven

parts.title: Commodities, species and commodity codes
parts.scope: The GET /commodities search and POST /commodities/species-check endpoints: how a trader's search finds commodities by code or name, how results are grouped into commodity groups and lines with their species, how commodity codes are matched, how the species check answers, and the MDM product calls behind them. MdmService and MdmClient are read in full; claim only their product, commodity and species methods. Stops at countries and ports (part 1) and shared error handling (part 3).
covers: GET /commodities: its route, every query parameter with its default and limit (search text, page, size and any other), how a search by code and a search by name are told apart and run, and every field of CommoditySearchResponse, CommodityGroup, CommodityLine and CommoditySpecies
Commodity identifiers: how commodity codes are matched, grouped and returned, and how species are attached to each commodity line
POST /commodities/species-check: its request and response fields, every rule SpeciesCheckService applies, and every answer it can give
The MdmClient calls /mdm/trade/product/search, /mdm/trade/product/commodities and /mdm/trade/product/commodities/{code}/species with their parameters and paging
What the 6 MDM product fixtures show about the shape of MDM commodity and species data (cattle, bison, dog, 0102), as evidence of today's MDM content only
Every test in the 7 test files listed that proves commodity or species behaviour (the MdmServiceTest product, commodity and species tests only), each as a claim of what is proven

parts.title: Service contract, rulings and missing lists
parts.scope: What holds across every list: the service's documented purpose and endpoints, its ADRs, how MDM failures reach a caller as HTTP errors, the MDM connection settings, and the scope's lists the service does not serve (transporters, document types, certification purposes), each recorded as a gap after searching the whole repo. Stops at each list's own behaviour (parts 1 and 2).
covers: The service's stated purpose, its list of endpoints and what callers it serves, from the README, AGENTS.md and the workspace repo page
ADR 0002 as a ruling: its decision and consequences verbatim; ADR 0001 only as the record-keeping rule
Every error a caller can receive: each exception, the HTTP status and response body GlobalExceptionHandler gives it, and how MdmErrorDecoder maps MDM responses, with the tests that prove each
The MDM settings in application.yml and MdmConfiguration that change what a caller receives (base URL, cache expiry, page sizes), not the plumbing

Three gaps, one each for transporters, document types and certification purposes: the scope expects the live-animals journey to read them, and the repo has no endpoint, model or MDM call for them; say where you looked (a repo-wide grep of src/ and the docs)
